questions.q: What is the relationship between this chapter's AI techniques and the production practices from Fabric & Real-Time Analytics Chapter 3?
options: AI is one more tool inside the already-established toolkit of testing, observability, incident response, and governance — it doesn't replace any of those practices
AI replaces the need for testing, observability, and incident response entirely
The production practices from Course 3 are now obsolete
AI and the production practices are unrelated to each other
questions.explain: Nothing in this chapter replaces the practices Fabric Chapter 3 established; AI speeds up specific tasks within them.

questions.q: Why does an AI-drafted RCA hypothesis depend on the observability practices from Fabric Lesson 52?
options: Observability is what actually produces the logs, metrics, and traces the RCA draft needs to say anything useful in the first place
Observability and RCA drafting are completely unrelated
AI can draft an RCA without any logs or data at all
Observability replaces the need for an RCA draft entirely
questions.explain: No logs means no useful draft — the production practice has to run before the AI-assisted step can add value.

questions.q: How do this chapter's guardrails (Lesson 56) relate to Fabric Lessons 61-62 on PII and secrets management?
options: The guardrails exist specifically to protect the same PII and secrets that those production practices already govern
The guardrails replace the need for PII and secrets management practices
They are unrelated topics that happen to appear in the same course
Secrets management only matters for AI workflows, not regular pipelines
questions.explain: The guardrails aren't a new AI-specific practice — they're the existing production practices that AI usage has to respect.

questions.q: What judgment calls does this lesson say AI cannot make, even with all this chapter's techniques applied?
options: What "production ready" means for a specific pipeline, how strict an SLA should be, and when an incident is actually resolved
Drafting a first-pass test case from a spec
Summarizing a log file's contents
Flagging an obviously invalid boundary value
questions.explain: Those decisions depend on business context an LLM was never given, and remain the engineer's responsibility.

questions.q: What does calling AI "one more tool in the toolkit" specifically rule out, per this lesson?
options: That AI could replace the established practices themselves rather than just speeding up tasks within them
That AI can be used for drafting test cases at all
That observability practices are still necessary
That a human should ever review AI-generated output
questions.explain: The phrase draws a firm line: AI augments execution of existing practices, it never substitutes for the practices or the judgment behind them.
